text:
ari: Hey all  question on adding my domestic partner to benefits. I got married-partnered this week and want to add them to health + dental. Workday only shows spouse options. Is there a different flow for domestic partners? Also do I need to submit any proof or affidavit?

Casey (People Ops): Congrats @ari!! We absolutely support domestic partner enrollment. You need to submit the Domestic Partner Affidavit (secure form) and a proof-of-cohabitation document (lease, utility bill, or joint bank statement) dated within the last 90 days. Fill the form here: https://redwood.example.com/hr/forms/domestic-partner-affidavit.pdf and upload docs via our secure upload: https://redwood.example.com/hr/secure-upload.

ari: Thanks! If I submit today, will coverage be retroactive to my partner's move-in date or my benefits effective date? The clinic needs coverage proof for an appointment next week.

BenefitsBot: BenefitsBot: Domestic partner enrollments processed after verified documentation are usually effective on the date we process the change. If you submit within 30 days of your event we can backdate to your original benefits effective date. For urgent proof, case managers can generate a temporary enrollment letter.

Casey (People Ops): To be concrete: submit the affidavit + proof, then ping me in DM. We aim to process within 3 business days. If you need the letter sooner tell me the clinic contact and appointment time and I can escalate.

ari: OK filing now. Quick related Q: I also set up a Dependent Care FSA and want to know if daycare receipts for earlier in the month can be reimbursed retroactively if partner is added after the service date?

zoe: (former benefits admin) DepCare FSA reimbursements are tied to the plan election period, but eligibility depends on when the dependent becomes eligible for coverage. If partner is retroactively enrolled to the start of the plan period, claims for eligible dependent care incurred during coverage should be reimbursable. You may need to submit a copy of the enrollment confirmation with the claim.

Payroll: Payroll: Note that FSA reimbursements are processed by HealthEquity and typically show as ACH to your bank on the next cycle after claim approval. For retroactive enrollments the vendor may request an adjusted eligibility feed.

ari: Great. One more: I already set 401(k) deferral to 6% and want to change to 10% mid-pay period. Can I do that immediately or does it wait until next payroll? And does changing pre-tax deferral affect FICA/tax withholding timing?

Casey (People Ops): 401(k) deferral changes via Workday are effective on the next payroll run after elections are processed by payroll. If you submit now and payroll processes elections before cutoff, it can apply next pay. It does not change your FICA rate but will reduce taxable wages for federal/state income tax starting when the deferral takes effect.

ari: Any cutoff times I should know? I don't want this to miss the upcoming Friday run.

Payroll: Payroll: Cutoff for deferral changes is 12:00pm PT two business days before payday. If you change after cutoff it will apply on the following run. If you need an exception we can sometimes accommodate with manual adjustments but only for limited cases. DM payroll with reason.

ari: Thanks. Last tiny thing: the office parking stipend line on my offer letter said $150/mo pre-tax. I just checked paystub and it's showing as taxable income. Is that expected?

Casey (People Ops): Parking stipends are usually taxable unless they are part of a qualified parking benefit under the commuter program. We offer a commuter pre-tax benefit up to the IRS limit if you enroll separately. Parking stipend recorded as reimbursement in payroll is taxable. If you intended commuter pre-tax, enroll here: https://redwood.example.com/hr/commuter-benefits and we can migrate future payments.

ari: Ah ok I'll enroll in commuter. If reimbursements already taxed, can payroll adjust prior periods?

Payroll: Payroll: We can only reclassify payments within the payroll system for open pay periods; historical taxes already filed cannot be fully reversed. If there's a material issue we can run a corrective payroll in coordination with tax advisors. Best to enroll before next month.

ari: Perfect. Uploaded affidavit/ docs and DM'd Casey. Thanks everyone for the quick answers! :partyparrot:
